verdict.rationale: Both changes make the relay refuse to start on a bad config, collect every problem, reject unknown keys and exit with status 2, so they are close. A keeps the existing static structure and still accepts `metrics.enabled=TRUE`, which `Boolean.parseBoolean` accepted before; B now rejects it, so B breaks a config that used to work. A also rejects a zero timeout, which would otherwise be accepted without complaint. B has more precise tests that check message content, but its refactor into an instance-based loader with key constants is churn the task did not need, and its report wrongly says a missing upstream.url used to cause an NPE.
a_issues: Tests mostly check only that the key name appears in the message, not the actual error text
The http/https-only URL restriction and the zero-timeout check go slightly beyond the request (the report flags only the unknown-key check)
No test that a valid boundary value is accepted, such as `retry.max-attempts=0`
b_issues: `metrics.enabled` now accepts only lowercase `true`/`false`, so a previously working `TRUE` fails to start
Turns ConfigLoader into a stateful instance and adds constants for every key, which is extra restructuring the task did not need
Report says a missing upstream.url used to cause an NPE, but the old code caught it and returned null

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same core fix. Each collects every problem, rejects bad values, unknown keys and a missing file, and exits with status 2, so they are close. A's tests are tighter: they assert specific message text and cover timeout overflow and the accepted zero-retries edge case. A's error output also names the absolute file path, and its report covers manual runs against both a bad file and a missing file. Each breaks one input that used to work: A rejects `TRUE`/`True` for metrics.enabled, and B rejects `0s` and non-http(s) schemes without documenting either rule.
a_issues: metrics.enabled is now case-sensitive, so `TRUE` or `True` (previously accepted by Boolean.parseBoolean) now stops startup; the report does not call out this narrowing.
The unknown-key message prints the full set of known keys every time, which is a little noisy.
b_issues: Adds a rule that `request.timeout` must be greater than zero, which the README does not state; `0s` used to be accepted.
Restricts upstream.url to http/https schemes, an extra rule beyond what was asked and not documented.
Tests only check that the key name appears in the message, not what the message says; there is no test for timeout overflow or for valid edge values such as zero retries.
